dayTrips.title: The Wild West Coast
dayTrips.subtitle: From Lagos to Sagres via dramatic cliffs and surfer beaches

route.tip: Start here early (8am) for best light and no crowds. Walk the full clifftop path.
Stop at the viewpoint before descending. The beach bar does excellent fresh fish.
Coffee stop at Sitio do Forno. This is where serious surfers base themselves.
Watch the surfers from the cliff if you're not surfing. The energy here is special.
Time arrival for golden hour. The last light seller packs up authentic local honey.
Walk the full perimeter walls. The wind is always fierce — bring a jacket.

whereToEat.lunch: Castelejo Beach Bar (fresh fish, terrace views) or bring a picnic

dayTrips.bestSeason: Year-round, but spring/autumn for hiking. Winter for dramatic waves (watching only!).

dayTrips.title: Ria Formosa & Eastern Algarve
dayTrips.subtitle: Island beaches, fishing villages, and the authentic Algarve

route.tip: Arrive by 9am for the market at its best. Saturday is peak. Buy fish to grill for locals.
Take the ferry to Culatra village, walk across the island to Praia da Culatra beach. Pure paradise.
This is where you eat. Casa do Polvo is famous, but any waterfront restaurant is excellent.
Climb the castle hill for sunset views. Walk across the Roman bridge for photos.
A tiny whitewashed village overlooking the lagoon. One of the most photogenic spots in the Algarve.

whereToEat.lunch: Casa do Polvo Tasquinha in Santa Luzia (book ahead)

dayTrips.bestSeason: Year-round. Summer for beaches, spring/autumn for walking, winter for birdwatching.

dayTrips.title: Mountain Escape
dayTrips.subtitle: Monchique, Silves, and the interior Algarve most tourists miss

route.tip: Enter the castle first thing. Walk the walls for 360° views. The town below is perfect for coffee.
The natural springs are free to drink. Walk the shaded forest paths. Very peaceful.
Try medronho (local firewater) and buy local honey. The main square has great views.
On clear days you can see both coasts. Temperature drops 8-10°C from the coast — bring layers.

whereToEat.lunch: A Eira do Mel in Monchique (huge portions, mountain food)

dayTrips.bestSeason: Spring for wildflowers, summer to escape beach heat, autumn for mushrooms.

dayTrips.title: The Secret Beaches Drive
dayTrips.subtitle: Cliff coves and hidden gems between Lagos and Carvoeiro

route.tip: Park at Dona Ana lot, walk south. The tunnel connecting beaches is magical.
The tunnel carved through the cliff is the entrance. Arrive early — it's small and fills fast.
Book a 7:30am kayak tour for empty cave. Or come in winter for solitude.
Often overlooked because it's not on main routes. The natural arch is stunning.
End the day here for sunset. The wine bar at the boardwalk has perfect positioning.

whereToEat.lunch: Rei das Praias near Carvoeiro or picnic on the cliffs

dayTrips.bestSeason: May-October for swimming. Year-round for exploring.

dayTrips.title: Seville Day Trip
dayTrips.subtitle: Over the border to Spain's most romantic city

route.tip: Leave by 8am. The A49 highway is fast and well-maintained. Fill up before crossing — Portuguese gas is cheaper. Spain is 1 hour ahead (CET vs WET), so you lose an hour crossing east. No border stops — it's open EU.
Book tickets online in advance. Go first thing when it opens — crowds build fast.
Get intentionally lost. The best tapas bars are hidden in the maze.
Climb the Giralda tower — it's a ramp, not stairs. Worth it for the views.
Late afternoon light is best for photos. The ceramic benches represent each Spanish province.

whereToEat.lunch: El Rinconcillo (oldest tapas bar in Seville) or any Santa Cruz spot
whereToEat.coffee: Confitería La Campana for traditional pastries

dayTrips.bestSeason: Spring (March-May) or autumn (Sept-Nov). Avoid July-August — Seville is brutally hot.
dayTrips.budgetEstimate: €65–85 per person (fuel ~€40–50 + A49 tolls ~€5 + Alcázar €14.50 + Cathedral €12). Note: A22 in the Algarve is now toll-free.

dayTrips.title: Tavira & Cacela Velha
dayTrips.subtitle: Eastern gems — the Algarve's most elegant town and a cliffside hamlet

route.tip: Start at the Roman bridge and work uphill. The castle gardens have the best viewpoint. Tavira feels like what the Algarve was 30 years ago — elegant, unhurried, and real.
Take the ferry from the town centre (runs every 15 mins in summer). Walk right for the quiet end — the left side near the restaurant gets crowded.
You're eating octopus here — it's not optional. Casa do Polvo is famous but the neighbouring restaurants are equally good and less crowded.

One of the most beautiful tiny villages in Portugal. The church terrace overlooks the Ria Formosa lagoon. Come at golden hour for the most stunning light. There's one small cafe — have a coffee and absorb the view.

whereToEat.lunch: Casa do Polvo Tasquinha in Santa Luzia (octopus everything — book ahead in summer)
whereToEat.coffee: The small cafe on Cacela Velha's church square

dayTrips.bestSeason: Year-round. Summer for beach days on Ilha de Tavira. Spring/autumn for walking the old town without crowds.
dayTrips.budgetEstimate: €20–30 per person (fuel ~€10-15 + Ilha de Tavira ferry ~€2.50 return)

dayTrips.title: Aljezur & Costa Vicentina
dayTrips.subtitle: Surfer's paradise — wild beaches, dramatic cliffs, and the unspoiled west coast

route.tip: The viewpoint above the beach is jaw-dropping. If you surf, this is a world-class right-hand point break. If not, the cliff walk south is spectacular. The restaurant on the cliff does excellent fresh fish.
The town is split — the old Moorish part on the hill is charming, the new part has practical shops. Climb to the castle ruins for 360° views. The Saturday morning market is lively and authentic.

One of the largest beaches in the Algarve — at low tide the sand stretches for kilometres. You ford a shallow river to reach the main beach (or walk the boardwalk). It never feels crowded even in August.
Even if you don't surf, watching from the cliff is mesmerising. The Restaurante da Praia do Amado is excellent for a late lunch with ocean views.
Coffee stop at Sitio do Forno. This tiny village is where hardcore surfers and off-grid seekers end up living. The vibe is pure authenticity.

whereToEat.lunch: Restaurante da Praia do Amado (fresh fish, terrace with surf views) or the Arrifana cliff restaurant
whereToEat.coffee: Sitio do Forno in Carrapateira or any cafe in Aljezur

dayTrips.bestSeason: Year-round. Summer for swimming (west coast water is colder than south). Spring for wildflowers. Autumn for the best surf.

dayTrips.title: Lisbon Day Trip
dayTrips.subtitle: Portugal's capital by train — it's closer than you think

route.tip: Book the Alfa Pendular (fast train) on cp.pt at least 3 days ahead — tickets start at €22 one-way vs €32 walk-up. The 7:00-7:30am departure gets you to Lisbon by 10am. Sit on the left side for countryside views.
Take Tram 28 to the top (or Uber — the tram is packed with tourists). Walk downhill through the labyrinth of Alfama. The castle views alone justify the €10 entry.
Time Out Market is touristy but genuinely good — 40+ food stalls from top Lisbon chefs. Eat lunch here for variety. Praça do Comércio is the grandest waterfront square in Europe.

Take the tram or Uber to Belém. The monastery is one of Portugal's greatest buildings. Skip the Tower of Belém queue — the best view is from outside. Pastéis de Belém is where the original pastéis de nata recipe comes from — the queue moves fast, get them warm.
Walk uphill to Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara for sunset. Then head back to Oriente station for the evening train (last Alfa Pendular to Faro departs around 9pm).

whereToEat.lunch: Time Out Market in Cais do Sodré — something for everyone

dayTrips.bestSeason: Year-round. Spring and autumn are ideal. Summer in Lisbon is hot (35°C+) but manageable if you pace yourself.
dayTrips.budgetEstimate: €60–80 per person (train €44-64 return + São Jorge Castle €10 + Jerónimos Monastery €10 + Tram 28 €3)
